title: Positioning Schema
strapline: Everything lined up, balanced on the edge, sorted into rows — the child for whom exactly where a thing goes really matters.
intent: Recognise positioning as a schema — a deep concern with where things go: lined up, balanced, ordered, on top, in a row.
Understand the learning inside it: order, sequence, one-to-one correspondence, symmetry and early pattern.
Read the perfectly lined-up cars and the food arranged just so as thinking, not fussiness — and never sweep it away.
Build fine placing control and the beginnings of sorting, matching and making patterns.
Respect the child's strong sense of order — and the big feelings when a careful line is disturbed.
implementation: Offer collections that invite arranging: cars, animals, blocks, stones, buttons, shells, loose parts on trays and along shelves.
Provide frames for order — grids, ice-cube trays, lines taped on the floor, tuff-tray borders, mirror tiles for symmetry.
Name the schema alongside them ('you've lined them all up in a row — every one facing the same way').
Photograph careful arrangements before tidy-up so the child's ordering is honoured and can be revisited.
Protect a line-up in progress from other children where you can, and offer calm words when an arrangement is knocked.
key_questions: How have you decided the order?
Which one comes next in your line?
Shall we line them up biggest to littlest?
Does each one have its own space in the tray?
Your row is so straight — how did you make it that neat?

impact.text: A child lines up, orders and arranges objects with care, placing each one deliberately just where it belongs.
Toddlers place small objects precisely into rows, grids and trays, fine control growing with each careful move.
Early pattern and sequence appear as children line things up by size, colour or kind and say what comes next.
Positioning explores space — on top, next to, in a row, along the edge — worked out through the hands.

enhancements: Ice-cube trays and grids for one-in-each-space sorting.
Long collections of matching objects — cars, stones, animals — for lining up.
A taped road or shelf edge that invites a straight, ordered line.
A mirror tile laid flat so arrangements double into symmetry.
A camera to photograph careful line-ups before they are tidied.

playing_exploring: The child arranges and orders on their own terms, deciding exactly where each thing goes.
Placing and lining up are done with focused, hands-on care.
active_learning: Toddlers return to an arrangement again and again, perfecting the order and the spacing.
creating_thinking: Children hold a rule in mind — same way, biggest first, one each — and place every object to match it.
